problem_statement.core_problem: Coding agents narrate success they did not achieve. An agent can claim a validation gate PASSed while the evidence file was never written, mock a system to make a check go green, or run a destructive command (git stash, pkill -f, checkout in a shared checkout) that silently breaks unrelated work — and none of this is visible while it happens or provable afterwards.
pain_points: Agent prose is unverifiable: PASS claims are not backed by artifacts on disk
Long autonomous runs are opaque — no live view of tool calls, hook decisions, token burn or dollar cost
Destructive shell commands in a shared repo or worktree have real blast radius
Local Claude Code settings (plugins, hooks, skills, env overrides) leak into runs and make them irreproducible
Post-hoc auditing requires reconstructing what happened from scrollback that is already gone
Validation reports written by the agent are self-graded
problem_statement.solution_approach: Wrap the Claude Agent SDK query loop in a runner that (1) appends a machine-readable runner contract to every plan so verdict lines are parseable, (2) independently verifies Capture: evidence files exist and are non-empty before accepting a PASS, (3) enforces configurable PreToolUse deny/warn rails, (4) streams every observation as a typed RunEvent into both an animated Ink cockpit and runs/<id>/ on disk, and (5) writes VALIDATION reports and ROADMAP status from its own observations rather than agent prose.

product_vision.statement: Vigil is the trust layer for autonomous coding agents: a cockpit that makes an agent run observable while it happens and provable after it ends. It never accepts a claim it has not independently verified — every PASS is backed by bytes on disk, every destructive action passes a rail, and every report is rendered from Vigil's own recorded observations rather than the agent's prose.
product_vision.north_star: A run that is reproducible, auditable and portable: any engineer can re-run the same plan on a clean machine, replay the recorded event stream, and reach the same verdict without trusting either the agent or the operator who ran it.
design_principles: Observer and enforcer, never executor — the agent does the work; Vigil constrains what it may do, what it must print, and what must exist before a claim is accepted
Evidence is bytes, not existence — presence is `bytes > 0`, never existsSync; an empty file created to satisfy a checklist does not count
One event spine — everything Vigil sees is a typed RunEvent appended to events.jsonl; the TUI, reports, replay and tail are all pure functions of that one stream
Reports from observation — VALIDATION.md and the ROADMAP status row are rendered from gates.json, and the contract forbids the agent from writing them
Clean agent by default — settingSources: [] so operator plugins, hooks, skills and env overrides never leak into a run
Degrade gracefully — no TTY, --plain or CI automatically drops the animation and emits a line-oriented log with the same information
Purity islands — reducer.ts and anim.ts have zero runtime imports, which is what makes the 18-case event fold unit-testable without a live SDK session
product_vision.differentiator: Every comparable tool logs what an agent said. Vigil is built around disbelieving it: the PASS→FAIL downgrade with a correction injected back into the live session is the product, and everything else is plumbing that makes that loop observable.

implemented_on_main.name: Evidence-gated verdict enforcement
implemented_on_main.detail: Parses VG-<id>: PASS|FAIL from the streamed text, resolves the gate's Capture: targets (globs with * and {a,b} alternation supported), and downgrades any PASS whose targets are missing or zero-byte, injecting a correction into the live session.

implemented_on_main.name: Runner contract injection
implemented_on_main.detail: Appends a machine-readable protocol block to every plan prompt demanding per-gate and per-plan verdict lines, asserting hard prohibitions (no mocking, no git stash, no checkout in main, no pattern kills, NODE_ENV unset) and forbidding the agent from authoring VALIDATION.md.

implemented_on_main.name: PreToolUse rails
implemented_on_main.detail: Seven configurable regex rails (five deny, two warn) evaluated against a flattened '<tool> <json input>' view, with every decision and its latency recorded as a hook event.
implemented_on_main.maturity: core, tested — but defaults are author-specific

implemented_on_main.name: Ink cockpit TUI
implemented_on_main.detail: React 19 + Ink 7 terminal cockpit: header, plan/gate pane, agent stream, tool cards, diagnostics, footer; six modal overlays; a modal keyboard state machine; responsive layout that stacks below 110 columns.
implemented_on_main.maturity: functional, ZERO automated coverage except anim.ts

implemented_on_main.name: Run artifact persistence
implemented_on_main.detail: Five artifacts per run under runs/<runId>/: append-only events.jsonl, tools/NNNN-<tool>.txt, gates.json, cost.json, session.json — the single source downstream for TUI, reports, replay and tail.

implemented_on_main.name: Reports generated from observation
implemented_on_main.detail: <NN>-VALIDATION.md and the matching ROADMAP status row are rendered from the recorded gate ledger on plan completion.
implemented_on_main.maturity: core, tested — but the 'Mock Violations' section is hardcoded and asserts a check the code never performs

implemented_on_main.name: Three approval modes
implemented_on_main.detail: auto / gates / all — gates presents every claimed PASS to the operator (rejection downgrades to fail), all blocks on every tool call. Switchable live from the TUI.
implemented_on_main.maturity: functional; only gates-mode has automated coverage

implemented_on_main.name: Replay, tail and runs inspection
implemented_on_main.detail: replay re-animates a recorded run through the real App at a speed multiplier; tail follows a live events.jsonl from another terminal; runs lists recorded runs with verdict, cost and event count.
implemented_on_main.maturity: functional, ZERO automated coverage; tail has a known byte/UTF-16 offset defect

implemented_on_main.name: Clean-agent isolation
implemented_on_main.detail: settingSources: [] by default so no operator plugins, hooks, skills or env overrides load; deterministic child env built as process.env minus unsetEnv, then cfg.env, then explicit overrides.
implemented_on_main.maturity: shipped in the most recent commit; ZERO automated coverage

implemented_on_main.name: Background health probes
implemented_on_main.detail: Interval HTTP and shell probes emitting probe events into the cockpit alongside the agent stream.
implemented_on_main.maturity: functional, ZERO automated coverage; schema permits a probe with neither url nor command

known_defects.issue: Secret redaction engine is built and tested but never wired — store.ts, session.ts and cli.ts on branch 005 have zero references to it. runs/ is never gitignored and tool artifacts store inputs and outputs verbatim.
known_defects.source: branch auto-claude/005, verified by git grep

known_defects.issue: A gate authored without an explicit `id` silently has no detectable verdict. GATE_RE demands a literal VG- prefix while the parser's fallback id is `${tag}-${n}` (e.g. validation_gate-4), which can never match. Silent failure, no warning.

The 'Mock Violations' section of VALIDATION.md emits a hardcoded string asserting a rails check the code never performs — a false negative by construction, in the one document whose stated purpose is observed truth.
maxBudgetUsd is accepted in config and handed to the SDK but never enforced locally. A runaway run is bounded only by maxTurns (default 400).

DEFAULT_RAILS hardcodes one machine's paths and services ('Desktop/OmniRoute', "Nick's real omp config", .omniroute/storage.sqlite), and setting `rails` in config REPLACES the defaults entirely rather than extending them.

`vigil tail` tracks byte offsets against a UTF-16 decoded string. Since plainLine emits ▶ ✓ ✗ and reports write ✓/✗, any non-ASCII content permanently desynchronises the tail and corrupts every subsequent line. It also re-reads the whole file every 500ms and never self-terminates on run.end.
New RunEvent variants are silently dropped by the UI — the reducer switch has no default case and no exhaustiveness guard, so an added variant compiles clean and never reaches the screen.

No prepare or prepublishOnly script, while bin/vigil.js imports ../dist/cli.js. Installing from git or publishing without a manual `npm run build` produces a binary that fails with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND.
CLI enum flags (--approvals, --log, --settings) are type-cast at the boundary without validation, so `--approvals bogus` propagates silently.
reducer.ts is documented as 'Pure; testable' but the private diag() helper mutates the array shared by the shallow copy.

Plan discovery is exactly two levels deep (phases/<dir>/<file>); more deeply nested plans are not found. ProbeSchema permits a probe with neither url nor command. Report gate classification uses id-prefix string matching rather than the parsed kind, and keeps only the first match per phase.

technical: Node >= 20 and pure ESM — no CommonJS consumers
Requires an external Claude Code executable on the machine; Vigil cannot run standalone
Coupled to @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk 0.3.261 pinned exactly at a pre-1.0 version; SDK message shapes and hook callbacks are an unstable surface
Terminal-only UI via Ink — no web dashboard, and animation requires a TTY plus config.animations plus absence of --plain
Verdict detection depends on the agent obeying the injected text contract; a model that reformats its output breaks enforcement
Evidence verification is filesystem-local — no remote or containerized evidence resolution
Config discovery is first-file-wins with NO merging, so a partial file silently gets schema defaults rather than lower-priority values
Single-run, single-process: no concurrency, no daemon, no multi-run aggregation
noUncheckedIndexedAccess is not enabled despite strict: true
process_and_project: Single author, 2 commits on main, no CI pipeline, no lint or format script, no LICENSE file, unpublished to npm
Feature work happens in .auto-claude worktrees on long-lived branches that are not being merged — integration debt is the dominant process risk
docs/ and .auto-claude/ are untracked, so the requirements baseline and all roadmap state live outside version control
No release process, no CHANGELOG, no versioning discipline beyond 0.1.0
Test suite is fast and real (no mocks) but covers roughly half the source; the CLI, config, replay, probes and TUI layers are unverified
product: Shipped defaults encode one machine's filesystem, ports and services, which blocks any second user
There is no path from zero to a first run — no init, no quickstart scaffolding, no example plan outside tests/fixtures
Reports claim a mock-violation check that does not exist, which undermines the product's central trust claim
Run artifacts capture secrets verbatim and runs/ is not gitignored
non_constraints: No performance or scale pressure — 1,722 lines of source, single-user, single-run; correctness and trust dominate over throughput
No backwards-compatibility obligation — unpublished, no external users, so breaking changes are cheap right now and will not stay cheap

risks.detail: 001, 004 and 005 all touch config.ts and cli.ts. Each additional change to main multiplies the three-way conflict cost, and the QA effort already spent gets revalidated or discarded.

risks.risk: Redaction looks done and protects nothing
risks.detail: A merged-but-unwired redactor would give the operator false confidence that runs/ is safe to share while tool artifacts still contain tokens verbatim. Do not merge 005 until store/session/cli actually call it.
The four docs/ files encode FR-1..FR-25 and NFR-1..NFR-9 with citations and are not in git. Losing them loses the only formal specification of what Vigil guarantees.
@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk is pinned at 0.3.261. Message shapes and PreToolUse hook semantics can change without notice, and session.ts (301 lines, the largest file) is where that breakage lands.

risks.risk: Contract compliance is a soft dependency
risks.detail: Enforcement rests on the agent printing VG-<id>: PASS|FAIL in a parseable form. A model change or a verbose formatting habit degrades enforcement silently rather than loudly.
Two commits, one contributor, no CI, no LICENSE, machine-specific defaults. The project currently cannot be picked up by anyone else without the merge of branch 001 plus an onboarding path.
